title: Test the specificity of Ardıç's tughra stroke parallels
statement: I compared the p. 84 glyph image and the p. 92 notebook and tughra reproductions in Ardıç (2025), https://www.turkicresearch.com/files/articles/4072.pdf, with scans of two independent comparators. This screening was unblinded. The glyph crop has an upright and a long horizontal sweep with a right-hand turn and loop. Ardıç proposes a rotated P and other components but gives several phonetic alternatives. The large notebook tughra shows nested left-hand loops, three upright shafts and long right-going strokes. The small signature on the same printed page is a denser group of crossings and loops. The published crop on p. 84 does not identify its folio. On Yale MS 408 f1r, at the start of the lowest paragraph, a separate Voynich example also shows an enlarged upright crossed by a long horizontal return stroke (https://collections.library.yale.edu/iiif/2/1006076/pct:14,61,24,9/850,/0/default.jpg). In the Vatican Greek Posthomerica manuscript Barb. gr. 166 (1476), f239r, the three intertextual flourishes also combine a long sweep, an upright crossing and loops (https://digi.vatlib.it/view/MSS_Barb.gr.166/0567). In the Marseille Latin charter of 10 March 1425, Archives départementales des Bouches-du-Rhône B 641 p. 8, the decorated opening letters include extended strokes and compact curved junctions. The notarial sign below has radiating axes with curled terminals, a different arrangement of similar graphic elements. Catalogue https://gams.uni-graz.at/archive/objects/o%3Acord.65e51e9a.e760.3984.b201.e90889083455/methods/sdef%3ATEI/get?locale=en and scan https://images.icar-us.eu/iiif/2/illum%2FIllUrk%2F1424-03-10_Marseille_AD_Bouche_du%20Rhone_B641_p8.jpg/full/1300,/0/default.jpg. These examples show how coarse stroke features can recur outside the proposed pairing. They leave the specificity of a fixed component correspondence and the independence of repeated matches open.
check: Locate the p. 84 glyph on an unmarked manuscript scan and preregister the component boundaries and any allowed rotations, mirroring and bridges. Sample matched connected marks in tughra, Voynich, Greek and Latin running hands and separate display marks by comparable stroke count, aspect ratio, and role. Mask provenance, have independent annotators trace loops, joins, uprights and turns with a fixed tolerance, then test the proposed component mapping on new marks and report cross-script confusion and rater agreement.
